issues.title: New regression test never exercises the _outgoing_queue_ready drain path
issues.verdictReason: con->send(eof) in sink_impl::close() resolves only after send_entry() completes and sets p->done, so by the time stream_close() runs, _outgoing_queue_ready is already a ready future; the new queue_drained wait at rpc.cc:562-569 is a no-op in this test and reverting it would not fail the test.
issues.scopeReason: The gap is in the new regression test added by this PR to cover its own fix.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Test doesn't exercise the queue-drain path in stream_close()

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: When stream_close() runs in this test, the eof entry has already finished, so queue_drained is ready and only the gate at rpc.cc:293 is exercised; dropping the drain at rpc.cc:557-570 would still pass even though a hook frame queued just before the mark can reach it.

issues.title: Claimed risk that base-case test aborts instead of cleanly failing
issues.verdictReason: SEASTAR_ASSERT (used in ~output_stream) is active in all build modes, not stripped by NDEBUG, so the premise is wrong; empirically reverting the fix and running the test 15 times always produced the clean BOOST_REQUIRE_MESSAGE failure at line 2030, never a crash/abort.
issues.scopeReason: Claim is about the reliability of the new test added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Base-case test failure mode depends on scheduling, may abort instead of throwing as…

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: The try/catch accepts the hook succeeding, and the 10 yield() calls don't force the batch-flush poller despite the comment, so outside debug builds base can abort in ~output_stream instead of failing with the BOOST message the commit claims; BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW(stream_send_empty_frame().get(), rpc::closed_error) would fail on base every time.

issues.title: Claimed non-determinism of the test's forced race window
issues.verdictReason: The test runs on loopback_socket.hh under a single-shard cooperative scheduler, so the ordering between the client's own stream_close() and any possible _error is deterministic by construction, not racy; running the base (pre-fix) code 15 times reproduced the exact same failure every time with no pass-through.
issues.scopeReason: Claim concerns the determinism of the new regression test's setup.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Claim that window is 'held open deterministically' is overstated

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: The server keeps draining while close() is parked, so the client's _error could be set first; base would then refuse via _error and pass, though this is unlikely in practice.

issues.title: Docs: reading a source until it throws is not always enough to close it
issues.verdictReason: source_impl::operator() (rpc_impl.hh:948) calls unmarshall() directly, unguarded; only stream_receive() failures or eof (rpc_impl.hh:961-972) route through close_source(), so a malformed-payload unmarshall exception propagates without ever calling close_source(), contradicting the new doc text.
issues.scopeReason: The inaccurate text is new documentation added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Docs wrongly say reading a source until it throws is sufficient to close it

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: The docs say reading until it 'throws' closes a source, but an unmarshall failure in process_one_buffer never calls close_source(), so an application that follows the docs and stops there never triggers stream_close().

issues.title: Docs overstate that the connection only shuts down once both halves close
issues.verdictReason: server::connection::abort_all_streams() (rpc.cc:1324-1331) directly calls abort() on every stream connection with no regard to sink/source closure state, and general I/O/loop errors do the same via stop_send_loop(), so the categorical claim is inaccurate as worded.
issues.scopeReason: The inaccurate text is new documentation added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Docs wrongly claim connection shuts down only once both halves are closed

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: Peer eof, loop errors, and abort_all_streams() all stop the connection without both halves being closed, contradicting the commit's claim of 'never shut down' otherwise.

issues.title: Comment misattributes cause of an exceptional _outgoing_queue_ready
issues.verdictReason: send_entry() failure always resolves its entry's done promise via set_value() (rpc.cc:333-339), never set_exception(); the chain can only become exceptional via withdraw(it, ex) called from a concurrently-running stop_send_loop(), not from 'an entry failing' to send.
issues.scopeReason: The comment is new text added by this PR's fix commit.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Comment wrongly says path is only exceptional if an entry failed

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: The comment states the path is '(exceptional if an entry failed)', but a failed send_entry calls abort() and then done.set_value(), not an exception.

issues.title: Comment overstates that nothing else waits on _outgoing_queue_ready
issues.verdictReason: stop_send_loop() (rpc.cc:225) still references _outgoing_queue_ready via when_all; it is harmless only because _stream_closing already prevents new pushes, making the value trivially ready, but the comment's 'nothing else waits' is imprecise.
issues.scopeReason: The comment is new text added by this PR's fix commit.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Comment wrongly claims nothing else waits on _outgoing_queue_ready

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: stop_send_loop() still waits on _outgoing_queue_ready in when_all (rpc.cc:225); it just now gets the ready placeholder.

issues.title: Comment overclaims only the trailing stop() can set _error during stream_close()
issues.verdictReason: A concurrently running stop_send_loop() (triggered by a loop error or abort_all_streams()) can call abort()/set _error=true while this stream_close() call's own drain-and-close is still in flight, before its own trailing stop() runs.
issues.scopeReason: The comment is new text added by this PR's fix commit.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Comment overclaims that _error is only set by the stop() that follows

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: abort() and loop errors can also set _error during the new drain wait, contradicting the comment's claim that only the following stop() sets it.

issues.title: Test's put(std::span) override lacks the SEASTAR_API_LEVEL guard, breaks API 7/8 builds
issues.verdictReason: data_sink_impl only declares the pure-virtual put(std::span<...>) when SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9 (iostream.hh:110-117); at API level 7/8 it declares put(net::packet) instead, so test_data_sink_impl::put(std::span<...>) override would fail to compile, unlike loopback_socket.hh:144-153 which guards both overloads. CMakeLists.txt:72-80 still documents/allows levels 7 and 8.
issues.scopeReason: The unguarded override is in the new test code added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: New put(std::span) test override lacks API-level guard, breaks build at API levels 7/8

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: The put(std::span) override has no #if SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9 guard, unlike loopback_socket.hh:144, so rpc_test stops compiling at API levels 7/8, which CMakeLists.txt still allows.

issues.title: close_entered_cv.wait() has no timeout, a stuck regression hangs the test
issues.verdictReason: condition_variable::wait() is called with a predicate but no duration; if a future regression means close() is never entered, this blocks indefinitely and only the outer test harness timeout (e.g. ./test.py's default 300s) would end it.
issues.scopeReason: The unguarded wait is in the new test added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: close_entered_cv.wait has no timeout, regression could hang until 300s harness timeout

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: A regression that never reaches close() hangs until the 300 second harness timeout because close_entered_cv.wait has no timeout of its own.

issues.title: An early assertion failure in the new test would abort rather than report cleanly
issues.verdictReason: If BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL(client_factory.hooks.size(), 2u) or any earlier check throws, the local sink variable unwinds unclosed, and ~sink_impl's SEASTAR_ASSERT(sink_closed()) (rpc_impl.hh:935) aborts the process instead of yielding a clean Boost.Test failure; deferred_close(sink) would avoid this but isn't used, matching the pattern in other stream tests in this file.
issues.scopeReason: The exposure is in the new test added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Early test assertion failure leaves sink unclosed, aborting the process instead of…

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: A failing BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL(hooks.size(), 2u) (or any earlier throw) drops the unclosed sink, and ~sink_impl's assert aborts instead of reporting; existing stream tests share this issue, and deferred_close(sink) would avoid it.

issues.title: const_cast used instead of a mutable member, inconsistent with existing file style
issues.verdictReason: hook_capturing_compressor_factory::negotiate() uses const_cast<hook_capturing_compressor_factory*>(this)->hooks.push_back(...) to mutate state from a const method, while the existing cfactory in the same file (rpc_test.cc:330) solves the identical problem with a mutable member.
issues.scopeReason: The inconsistent pattern is in the new test helper added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: const_cast used in hook_capturing_compressor_factory::negotiate instead of existing…

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: The same file uses a mutable member (cfactory, rpc_test.cc:330) for this purpose elsewhere, making the const_cast inconsistent.

issues.title: New test's put(std::span) dependency limits clean backport to pre-2025-10 branches
issues.verdictReason: The fix commit (f545c28a) only touches src/rpc/rpc.cc and include/seastar/rpc/rpc.hh and is self-contained, but the regression test relies on data_sink_impl::put(std::span), an API-9 feature, so it would not apply unmodified to branches predating that API; no backport claim is actually made anywhere in this PR though, so this is informational rather than a defect in the PR as submitted.
issues.scopeReason: The PR makes no backport claim; this is speculative analysis of a scenario the PR does not address.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Backport claim only partly holds for branches lacking put(std::span)

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: The test's put(std::span) (added 2025-10) won't apply to branches from 2023-10 to 2025-10 which have the bug, though the fix commit itself is self-contained.

issues.title: PR commits lack a DCO Signed-off-by trailer
issues.verdictReason: None of the three PR commits (69da8f5b, 5e25ebdb, f545c28a) has a Signed-off-by line, and doc/contributing.md:6-10 asks for one; however sampling 20 recent commits on main shows only 1 carries a sign-off, so this is the repo's prevailing (if non-compliant) practice, not something this PR changed.
issues.scopeReason: Nearly all commits in this repository's history already lack the sign-off; the PR did not introduce or worsen the gap.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Commits lack Signed-off-by DCO line required by contributing docs

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: None of the three commits has a Signed-off-by line, though doc/contributing.md asks for a DCO sign-off (though repo history mostly skips it).

issues.verdictReason: All three PR commits end with 'Co-Authored-By: Claude ...' trailers, confirmed by git log; this matches a pattern already present on several existing commits on main (e.g. 329cf927, e8d7b5c7), so it is consistent with this repository's existing practice rather than unique to this PR.
issues.scopeReason: The same trailer pattern already exists on multiple commits in this repository's history, so this PR did not introduce the practice.

issues.verdictReason: origin now points at github.com/dkropachev/ironweave (repointed by 5cc62de6), and 'Fixes #3663 / Refs #3653' in f545c28a's message would auto-close issues in that repo on merge; whether those issue numbers actually correspond to real, matching issues there or were meant for upstream scylladb/seastar can't be settled without a GitHub lookup, which isn't available in this environment.
issues.scopeReason: The Fixes/Refs references are part of this PR's own commit message.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Fixes/Refs issue links may resolve against the wrong repo, risking auto-close of wrong…

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: Fixes #3663 / Refs #3653 resolve against dkropachev/ironweave, whose links base 5cc62de6 repointed; they likely mean upstream issues but this couldn't be confirmed because the fetch failed, and if so, merging could auto-close the wrong local issue.

issues.title: Self-rejected: _stream_closing claimed as a hazard with enqueue_zero_frame
issues.verdictReason: client::enqueue_zero_frame() (rpc.cc:866) is only ever invoked once, from the client's own connect/constructor path (rpc.cc:977), strictly before any stream sink/source exists, so it can never race with stream_close() setting _stream_closing; confirmed no other call site exists.
issues.scopeReason: The flag under discussion is new, added by this PR's fix commit.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: _stream_closing flag claimed as a hazard

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: The _stream_closing flag is not a hazard because enqueue_zero_frame only runs from the constructor.

issues.title: Self-rejected: size/complexity of the test's socket wrapper classes
issues.verdictReason: The wrapper hierarchy (test_data_sink_impl, test_connected_socket_impl, test_socket_impl) is the minimum needed to intercept data_sink::close() at the socket layer for this specific race, since rpc::connection offers no other hook at that level; the size is justified by what the regression requires.
issues.scopeReason: The wrapper classes are new test code added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Size of test's socket wrappers questioned

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: The size of the test's socket wrappers is justified.

issues.title: Self-rejected: parent-client connection claimed to share the same send race window
issues.verdictReason: stop_send_loop() sets _error = true as its very first statement (rpc.cc:199), before it later closes the write buffer in its own when_all().then() continuation (rpc.cc:225-232); connection::send()'s '!_error' check therefore already closes this window for the parent connection, unlike stream_close() which deliberately defers setting _error.
issues.scopeReason: Confirmed no equivalent defect exists on the parent-connection path; nothing for this PR to fix there.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Parent-client connection claimed to have an equivalent race window

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: The parent-client connection has no equivalent window, because stop_send_loop() sets _error before closing.

issues.title: Self-rejected: claimed use-after-free on test_sink_state st
issues.verdictReason: release_close is a shared_promise<> owned by the same test_sink_state as the data_sink_impl that holds a reference to it; the test always either resolves it with set_value() or lets the enclosing lambda's own synchronous .get() calls flush all outstanding continuations before st goes out of scope, so no continuation observable outside the test's own scope can outlive st.
issues.scopeReason: The state in question is new test code added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Audit's claimed use-after-free on st does not happen

reportedAsByRun.rafp-native-controller-ironweave-2026-10: The audit's use-after-free on st doesn't happen: the broken shared_promise resolves the parked close.
